## What it is

Petty-cash receipts for a group of restaurants. Staff photograph receipts, Claude reads
the shop, date and total, staff check and tag each one, and a manager emails the month's
ledger as an xlsx file to the head of department.

It runs locally as a small web app for now; AWS comes next.

## What I built

Many small businesses in Japan still operate their monthly budgeting using data manually
entered by fatigued shop employees who often aren't trained in spreadsheet formats and
standards, leading to the digital equivalent of a hoarder's cluttered file system.

This project aimed to address these pain points in the simplest manner possible to reduce
error at the entry stage by employees, and to reduce the headache for managers who would
often spend hours untangling a spreadsheet that has had its formatting and save encoding
ruined by inconsistent software across multiple computers.

## How it works

- A model (Claude Haiku or Sonnet) extracts the shop, date and total from each photo,
  and the result is validated before staff see it.
- An evaluation command scores the extractors against hand-labelled sample photos.
